assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identification of GLP-1 as an incretin and its translation into long-acting agonists has produced a clear physiological discovery with transformative therapy for type 2 diabetes and obesity, with documented cardiometabolic benefits. Importance, originality and breadth of impact are exceptional.
assessment.attribution: Holst (physiology of GLP-1 secretion and action) and Drucker (intestinotropic and metabolic actions, translation) are central; Knudsen led the design of acylated long-acting analogues (liraglutide, semaglutide) that made the biology a medicine. Mojsov's sequence/activity contribution and the work of others (e.g. Habener, not credited here) complicate a three-person limit; the credit split between discovery and drug design is a real choice.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent replication, multiple large outcome trials and widespread clinical use make the science mature; timing is strong given the scale of therapeutic use.
uncertainties: Fair allocation among Mojsov, Drucker, Holst and Knudsen is unresolved, and a discovery-only configuration may differ from a discovery-plus-drug configuration.
Longer-term safety and effects beyond weight and glycemia are still accumulating; I cannot verify the latest outcome data independently.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Light-gated microbial opsins turned into tools for millisecond, cell-type-specific control of excitable cells gave neuroscience a causal method that reshaped circuit analysis across species. The conceptual and methodological originality is high and the impact is broad, though it is mainly a research tool, with clinical use still emerging (e.g. retinal restoration).
assessment.attribution: Nagel and Hegemann (with Bamberg) identified and characterised channelrhodopsins; Deisseroth and Boyden demonstrated neuronal control and drove adoption; Miesenboeck made earlier genetically targeted photoactivation. A three-person prize must leave out at least three well-credited contributors. Proposed trio balances discovery of the channel and its neuronal deployment.
assessment.maturity: More than fifteen years of widespread independent use; the core claims are firmly confirmed. Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Exclusion of Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenboeck is contentious.
Therapeutic translation is early, so the case rests on enabling-method impact.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered T cells have produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and opened a new class of living therapies. The discovery is a clear, clinically validated advance with strong lasting impact and expanding indications such as autoimmunity.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain contributed early CAR design with co-stimulation, June led the first clinical successes in leukemia, and Rosenberg pioneered adoptive cell transfer and gene-modified T cells in patients. Other contributors (e.g. Eshhar, Brenner, Gross) are not on the credited list, so I cannot assess them from this list.
assessment.maturity: Several approved products and years of follow-up confirm efficacy; toxicity and access limits remain, but the principle is stable and recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Whether early conceptual work by uncredited contributors deserves recognition is outside the supplied credit.
Long-term safety, secondary malignancies and solid-tumor efficacy remain open.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identification of cGAS as the cytosolic DNA sensor producing cGAMP, activating STING, defined a central innate-immune pathway relevant to infection, autoimmunity, cancer and ageing. It is a clear mechanistic discovery with wide conceptual impact.
assessment.attribution: Chen's biochemical purification of cGAS and discovery of cGAMP as a second messenger are decisive. Barber's STING work and the Ishikawa, Sun and Wu contributions matter; a single-laureate or a Chen plus STING-discoverer configuration is possible, but only the supplied names can be used. I propose Chen alone as the most defensible, noting that Barber's STING discovery may support a second laureate.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed across laboratories; therapeutic translation (agonists, antagonists) is still early, so clinical maturity is partial.
uncertainties: Credit between the STING discovery and the cGAS-cGAMP discovery is unresolved.
Clinical benefits are not yet established.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Virus-like particle HPV vaccines are a rare example of a basic discovery translated into cancer prevention, with population-level reductions in infection, cervical precancer and cancer. Clarity and impact are very high, although a 2008 prize already recognised the discovery of HPV as a cause of cervical cancer.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller developed L1 VLP assembly and its immunogenicity; Frazer contributed to the Australian VLP work and vaccine development. Contributions of other groups (e.g. Zhou, Kirnbauer) are not on the credited list and I cannot judge them.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, with real-world effectiveness data in several countries; recognition would be timely.
uncertainties: Parallel invention and patent disputes complicate credit.
Interaction with the prior HPV-cervical cancer prize may affect perceived novelty.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Massively parallel sequencing reduced the cost of genome sequencing by orders of magnitude and underlies modern genomics, cancer and rare-disease diagnostics, and infectious-disease surveillance. The impact is enormous, though it is a technology prize case and the 'discovery' is multi-part.
assessment.attribution: The credited trio's sequencing-by-synthesis and clonal-cluster approach is a coherent configuration, but other sequencing technologies (pyrosequencing, polony, ligation, nanopore) and companies also contributed, and the supplied credit may not capture that.
assessment.maturity: Technology is firmly established and widely validated; recognition is timely though a prior chemistry/physiology-or-medicine fit and the Chemistry prize (2020s) overlap are possible.
uncertainties: Attribution is disputed among competing platforms.
Fit to Physiology or Medicine versus Chemistry is uncertain; I cannot verify prior prizes for related technology.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery of TOR as the target of rapamycin and its role as the central regulator of cell growth and nutrient response links metabolism, growth, ageing and disease and led to approved drugs. Importance is high and the concept is clear.
assessment.attribution: Hall identified TOR genes and their function in yeast; Schreiber's work on FKBP12-rapamycin and mTOR binding was decisive for target identity; Sabatini's mammalian mTOR work is important but I treat the full credit conservatively. Credit across Hall, Schreiber and Sabatini is partially unresolved and Brown/Heitman (not listed) also contributed.
assessment.maturity: Highly confirmed with decades of replication; clinical benefits (transplant, oncology) exist but broader promised benefits remain limited.
uncertainties: Allocation among Hall, Schreiber, Sabatini and uncredited contributors is unresolved.
Some ageing and metabolic claims remain unproven.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Splice-switching antisense oligonucleotides that raise SMN protein led to nusinersen, the first disease-modifying therapy for spinal muscular atrophy, converting a fatal infantile disease into a treatable one. The mechanistic insight and clinical effect are clear and, as a motor-neuron disease treatment, concrete.
assessment.attribution: Krainer identified the splicing basis and ISS-N1 target; Bennett led the chemistry and development of the oligonucleotide. The two-person configuration is coherent, though clinical trial investigators and others (e.g. Hua, Adrian Krainer's collaborators) are not credited.
assessment.maturity: Several years of clinical follow-up with strong evidence, though durability and comparison with gene therapy are still maturing; recognition could be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Contribution of other splicing and antisense researchers cannot be assessed from the supplied credit.
Long-term outcomes and relative merit versus other SMA therapies are still being established.
